newsitem.title: FRANCE: French AIDS patients treated with new type of drug.
newsitem.headline: French AIDS patients treated with new type of drug.

text.p: French AIDS patients are being treated with a new class of drugs known as protease inhibitors, with more than 20,000 infected individuals now taking them, the government said on Wednesday.
Protease inhibitors work by preventing the AIDS virus leaving a patient's DNA and invading the rest of the body.
"Everything possible has been done to assure the availability of these new therapies," Secretary of State for Health Herve Gaymard told a meeting of the French cabinet.

When the new drugs, typically taken in combination with other AIDS drugs, first became widely available last year, French officials complained that their makers appeared to be focusing on the American market and failing to allocate supplies for Europe.
Among protease inhibitors are invirase (trade name saquinavir) made by F. Hoffman-La Roche RO.CZg.S, Norvir (ritonavir) made by Abbott Laboratories and Crixivan made by Merck and Co Inc.

France is the European nation hardest hit by the AIDS epidemic, with 50,000 reported cases of the disease, 30,000 deaths and 110,000 people who have tested positive for AIDS virus infection, Gaymard said.
